enquiry: We manufacture tablets from a powder blend containing an active pharmaceutical ingredient and excipients. Laboratory checks tell us whether the blend is on target, but results arrive after the material has moved through the press. We want to assess whether a fiber based measurement in the feed frame could follow API concentration changes. Our first pilot should compare reasonable measurement options before we commit to production equipment.

clarification_questions.question: What operational action or automated control decision will be triggered when real-time API concentration changes are detected in the feed frame?
clarification_questions.why: Determines the required data rate, response time, and automation integration path.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Operational goal is real-time monitoring and out-of-specification rejection or process alarming rather than automated feedback loop control.

clarification_questions.question: What is the specific API and excipient chemistry, what is the nominal API concentration, and over what concentration range must variations be tracked?
clarification_questions.why: Dictates whether NIR reflection, Raman, or a combination is required based on chemical selectivity and sensitivity (trace/ppm vs major percentage).
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening on representative blend samples establishes whether the API is at percentage or trace levels and identifies distinct spectral bands.

clarification_questions.question: What are the particle size distribution, color, and optical properties of the blend, and do excipients exhibit background fluorescence?
clarification_questions.why: Scattering effects dominate powder optics and Raman applicability depends on whether excipients or API fluoresce.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Sample is an opaque scattering powder blend requiring diffuse reflection optics or Raman backscattering; potential fluorescence background will be verified during initial lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: What are the physical feed frame conditions, including paddle rotation speed, powder filling level, vibration, temperature, and required cleaning/sanitization protocols?
clarification_questions.why: Governs probe window material, fouling mitigation, optical sampling geometry, and hygienic mechanical design.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Standard rotary feed frame operating at ambient room conditions requiring a robust, cleanable sanitary probe interface.

clarification_questions.question: Where can the probe be mounted on the feed frame (e.g., existing inspection port or custom viewport), and what is the physical distance to the intended analyzer location?
clarification_questions.why: Determines probe form factor, optical interface (direct contact window vs non-contact collimator), and fiber cable length and routing constraints.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point is an optical window on the feed frame top cover or side wall, with distance to analyzer unknown until site inspection.

clarification_questions.question: What current laboratory reference method is used for release testing, and what is its measurement precision and turnaround time?
clarification_questions.why: Establishes the ground-truth benchmark and uncertainty threshold against which single-method and combined optical calibrations must be validated.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method is off-line HPLC or equivalent chromatographic assay with turnaround on the order of hours.

clarification_questions.question: What are the required measurement accuracy, update interval, and target timeframe or budget for the pilot evaluation?
clarification_questions.why: Guides feasibility screening priorities between a single-method instrument and multi-method exploration.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pilot begins with laboratory feasibility screening comparing single-method models against the reference assay, scaling up to an in-situ feed frame trial only after model validity is proven.
